title: 10 Orvita: enterprise clinical AI hero
strengths: The product UI is specific and credible: a ward watchlist with bed, patient, risk score bar, 12-hour sparkline, signals (RR up, Lactate, SpO2) and status pills; the 'Why Orvita flagged Bed 12' card cites three sources with timestamps
Customer logos sit in equal cells with hairline dividers under a factual label ('Trusted at 41 health systems across 9 countries'), the more credible treatment
Instrument Sans with Geist Mono for timestamps; one teal, risk colours reserved for the data
slop_signals: 'New  Sepsis Watch validated across 41 hospitals ->' pill badge above the headline
Headline mixes weights to emphasise 'needs you next.'; the bold-phrase trick
Two buttons ('Book a clinical demo' filled, 'Read the validation study' outlined) and two check-mark reassurances (EHR, HIPAA · SOC 2 Type II) beneath
Three product fragments float at different offsets with soft shadows (the watchlist, the explanation card over it, a risk chart top right); the explanation card hides part of the table
Six invented hospital logos (St. Aldric, Northvale Medical, Kestrel Bay...) in five different type styles
Headline left, product right, logo row below: the enterprise template in full
fixes: Show one product frame face-on, with the explanation card docked inside the UI as a side panel, so nothing floats or overlaps
Remove the pill badge; set the validation fact as the sub-line's first sentence
One weight in the headline; one button; move the compliance line into the footer
Replace the logo row with the validation line or a single named health system plus the study citation, until real logos exist

references.what: Healthcare AI hero: serif headline left, one dark product panel right, one button, a logo row below with a small label; the 'New' note lives in the nav, not above the headline
Headline with a second phrase in grey rather than bold; numbered steps instead of floating cards
Customer logos in equal hairline cells; our row follows this and it is the strongest part
Enterprise hero with small buttons and the logo row directly under the headline; shows buttons at a quieter scale
A health-systems logo strip floating without cells, which reads weaker; what to avoid
